// Experience

My projects and
experiences throughout my studies

Revolve NTNU · Formula Student
2023, 2024, 2027
Chassis Structural (2027) · Chassis Design (2024) · Front Wing (2023)

2027: Structural design and analysis of the chassis, keeping within Formula Student rules while optimising for weight and stiffness. Used Python and FEA in the design process, validated through physical testing.

2024: Designed and modelled the monocoque in Solidworks, working closely with the mechanical and electrical groups. Revamped the monocoque-battery integration, cutting mounting time from 25 minutes to 5. Responsible for producibility, including tooling and mould design.

2023: Designed and produced the front wing package, covering both aerodynamics and manufacturing. Built moulds in MDF, aluminium, and 3D-printed polymers for CFRP manufacturing.

Associate Manufacturing Engineer · Summer & Part-Time

Three summer internships and two part-time remote positions in between, supporting manufacturing engineers. Designed fixtures and other manufacturing aids in NX CAD for a range of production processes, including CNC mill-turning, heat treatment, and welding.

Propulse NTNU
2025
Lead Outer Structure

Led the design, dimensioning, and production of the rocket's outer structure and fins, cutting weight by 20% while maintaining the same structural strength. Designed and simulated monolithic CFRP fins in Abaqus, and planned all manufacturing processes and moulds. It was the first rocket launch from Norway.

// About

About me

I'm an aspiring mechanical engineer finishing my MSc at NTNU, graduating spring 2027, specialising in product development and materials. My work covers design, FEA, manufacturing, and materials.

Three seasons with Revolve NTNU took me from designing the front wing in 2023, to modelling the monocoque in 2024, to being responsible for structural design and FEA of the chassis in 2027. The monocoque I designed helped win Revolve's first-ever competition victory, at Formula Student Netherlands in 2024, also a first for Norway.

In 2025 I led the outer structure and fin design for Propulse NTNU's rocket, cutting weight by 20% without losing structural strength. It was the first rocket launch from Norway.

Three summers and two part-time periods at GKN Aerospace had me designing fixtures and manufacturing aids in NX, for processes like CNC milling, heat treatment, and welding.

Won NTNU's TMM4163 Design and Production for Additive Manufacturing design competition by creating the strongest design.

Outside engineering, I boxed at a top level, winning gold at the Norwegian Championships (NM) in 2017 and silver in 2018.
